title: Pooling nitrate residuals cut error with immediate sample access, but not with a 14-day delay, at two Gulf outlets in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether recent nitrate residuals from the other river branch improve same-day estimates beyond own-site sample history. We used USGS release 3.0 and 767 sampled site-dates at St. Francisville and Melville in water years 2000-2025. Baseline fits used earlier years only. A fixed equal average of decayed own and other residuals reduced equal-site squared log error by 19.45%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was 11.89% to 25.41%. With a 14-day access delay at both sites, pooling increased error by 3.73%, with limits of 0.84% to 7.78%. The donor sample was newer on 81.10% of primary dates. A later half-own control did not explain the gain. The result supports useful shared information under immediate access, but not the same rule under the tested delay. Actual release times are unknown. Sparse sampling, two related branches, simple models and conditional intervals limit inference. This test does not establish a transport cause, daily load accuracy or hypoxia forecast skill. Public-domain inputs, source hashes, code, all predictions, resampling evidence, a numerical audit and a figure are included.

display.caption: Nitrate residual pooling against own-site memory. Positive values mean less error. Intervals condition on the observed record. The 14-day sample delay reverses the primary gain.
